sources.entry: Asterisk - Easy to use but advanced IP PBX system, VoIP gateway and conference server. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 C/deb

summary.one_liner: Asterisk is an open source PBX and telephony toolkit that acts as middleware between internet and telephony channels, supporting SIP/VoIP and traditional PSTN hardware.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Asterisk as an Open Source PBX and telephony toolkit bridging Internet telephony and PSTN/TDM channels at the bottom with telephony applications at the top. It states that most users run VoIP/SIP, but it also supports analog and digital interfaces through supported hardware such as Sangoma interface cards, Xorcom Astribank channel banks, and any full-duplex sound card supported by PortAudio. The README gives a build workflow using ./configure, make menuselect, make, make install, and make samples, then launching with asterisk -vvvc for a CLI console. Configuration files use a common sectioned format with ';' comments. The README also covers operational needs: keeping system time synced via ntpd/ntpsec, chronyd, or systemd-timesyncd, and raising file descriptor limits for high call volumes. It names Linux as the primary platform and says Mac OS X and BSD variants have been ported with reported success.
use_cases: connect analog or digital telephony lines to IP telephony
route calls between SIP phones and PSTN trunks
how_to_run: Read the documentation and the security considerations before configuring a server
./configure (run ./contrib/scripts/install_prereq install if dependencies are missing, then rerun ./configure)
make menuselect (optional: select modules and check dependencies)
make install, then make samples to install sample configs (overwrites existing configs)
asterisk -vvvc to start in foreground with a CLI console
notable: Supports SIP, IAX2, and H.323 signaling alongside PSTN hardware interfaces
Modular build with make menuselect for choosing optional modules
Includes contrib/scripts/install_prereq to install build dependencies on common distributions
Command-line console (CLI) for runtime control and help via core show help
caveats: README tells users to read the security considerations document before running a server
Sensitive to large system clock jumps, which can break SIP registrations; requires a time sync service
Primarily developed and tested on GNU/Linux; other OSes are reported to work but are less certain
